identity.title: Navigating the Latent Space Dynamics of Neural Models

problem.claim: The paper asks how neural models’ latent representations can be interpreted and analyzed as dynamics on a latent manifold.

contributions.claim: It derives a latent vector field for autoencoders by iteratively applying the encoding-decoding map, without additional training.

It proposes using this vector field as a representation for analyzing model and data properties, including training-stage generalization and memorization, data-free extraction of parameter-encoded prior knowledge, and trajectory-based out-of-distribution detection.
It reports validation on vision foundation models to demonstrate applicability and effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by interpreting neural models as dynamical systems acting on the latent manifold and by using the induced vector field as a model representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that standard training procedures lead to attractor points emerging in the latent vector field.
The authors report validation of the approach on vision foundation models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural networks are described as mapping high-dimensional data into structured representations in a lower-dimensional latent space.
The paper reframes neural models as dynamical systems operating on the latent manifold.
For autoencoders, repeated encoding and decoding implicitly define a latent vector field without extra training.
The authors associate standard-training inductive biases with attractors and propose the vector field for model and data analysis.
The abstract lists analyses of training regimes, data-free prior extraction, and out-of-distribution identification, followed by validation on vision foundation models.

source_observation.claim: The paper turns an iterated, already-defined model operation into an analyzable latent-space object, then maps that object to several analysis tasks.

lessons.interpretation: This can make a proposed analysis feel concrete by exposing an intermediate representation that connects mechanism to multiple uses.
lessons.application: When a model has a natural repeated transformation, define its induced state-space structure explicitly and link each claimed use to that structure.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the transformation has no meaningful iteration or when the induced states cannot be interpreted reliably.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, baselines, datasets, or evaluation conditions for the reported validation or effectiveness.
It does not specify how attractors are detected, how trajectories support out-of-distribution identification, or what is meant by extracting prior knowledge.
The abstract does not establish that the proposed representation outperforms alternative analyses.
